key_insight: Materials GNNs can achieve similar final accuracy with very different amounts of trainable parameter-space freedom, and random-subspace recovery curves expose that hidden dependence.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a model-selection and robustness test beyond accuracy, helping identify architectures that are easier to optimize under constrained capacity or weaker training conditions.
method: Train CGCNN, ALIGNN, and DimeNet++ in randomly oriented parameter subspaces.
Measure how performance recovers as more independent trainable degrees of freedom are restored.
Compare recovery across six materials-property prediction tasks, plus dataset-size and width sweeps.
evidence_signal: Across six tasks, the recovery curves show that metallic classification and log-bulk-modulus are robust to strong dimensional restriction, while phonon prediction is the most sensitive and band-gap/formation-energy depend more on architecture and dataset size.
watch_item: Random-subspace results depend on the chosen training setup and subspace sampling, so the fractional-dimension thresholds should be interpreted as comparative diagnostics rather than universal constants.
paper_title: Measuring trainable degrees of freedom in materials graph neural networks: a random-subspace intrinsic dimension analysis
